newsitem.title: USA: Allied Signal posts record third-quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Allied Signal posts record third-quarter profit.

text.p: Allied Signal Inc. Wednesday posted a record profit of $253 million for the third quarter on stronger sales by its aerospace and engineered materials divisions.
The company said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 rose 17 percent to $253 million, or 90 cents a share, from the record $217 million, or 77 cents a share, it earned a year ago.
Allied Signal said the results marked its 19th consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings increases.

The company said sales in the quarter slipped to $3.3 billion from $3.5 billion, primarily because of the sale of its braking business in April. Excluding the braking business, third-quarter sales expanded by 10 percent, it said.

"Our 17 percent increase in net income and substantial progress in productivity have put us well on our way toward achieving a 15 to 17 percent increase in earnings for 1996," Chairman Lawrence A. Bossidy said in a statement.
Allied Signal, based in Morris Township, N.J., said net income for its newly reconfigured Automotive sector was up 82 percent, Aerospace was up 21 percent and Engineered Materials gained 2 percent.
The company said the Aerospace sector benefited from the continued rebound of the commercial aviation original equipment market and from strength in the military and commercial aftermarkets.
Aerospace net income rose to a record $98 million from $81 million as sales increased to a record $1.5 billion from $1.3 billion, the company said.

Gains in the Automotive sector resulted from increased passenger car and light truck production in North America and Europe and from productivity improvements, which more than offset decreased production of medium- and heavy-duty trucks and a soft aftermarket, the company said.

Automotive net income rose to $40 million from $22 million as sales grew to $891 million from $848 million, the company said. The unit makes a wide variety of automotive components -- from safety systems and turbochargers to filters and spark plugs.

Sales and net income figures for 1995 excluded results of the divested braking business. Including the braking business, the Automotive unit had net income of $45 million in 1995 on sales of $1.3 billion.
Allied Signal said that in the Engineered Materials sector, strong volume growth in polymers and speciality chemicals was partially offset by weakness in electronic materials.
The company's stock lost 62.5 cents to $64.125 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
